- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00); cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true outcome if sentiment was high.
- Forecast tends to lag in early days of the 30-day horizon; adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast for days 1–5 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% in the reversal window.
- Model underestimates in high-sentiment, low-history-variability periods; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is high and recent prices are stable.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong trend, don’t extrapolate beyond 2–3% beyond that trend unless sentiment confirms.
